definitions.explanation: Going against reason or fairness; irrational and difficult to accept.

examples.japanese: {理不尽|りふじん}な{要求|ようきゅう}に{困|こま}っている。
なぜ{私|わたし}だけ{怒|おこ}られるのか{理不尽|りふじん}だ。
examples.english: It's unfair that only I get scolded.

examples.japanese: {理不尽|りふじん}な{扱|あつか}いに{抗議|こうぎ}した。

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{理|り} (reason) + {不尽|ふじん} (not exhaustive, lacking) → lacking reason = unreasonable

FORMS:
・{理不尽|りふじん}な{要求|ようきゅう} - unreasonable demand
・{理不尽|りふじん}な{扱|あつか}い - unfair treatment
・{理不尽|りふじん}さ (noun) - unreasonableness

NUANCE:
{理不尽|りふじん} expresses strong feelings about something that violates basic fairness or logic. Often used when someone feels wronged or sees injustice.

RELATED WORDS:
・{不条理|ふじょうり} - absurd, irrational
・{無理|むり} - unreasonable (less formal)
・{横暴|おうぼう} - tyrannical, overbearing
